question: What is a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre?
expected_answer: A vessel which from the nature of her work is restricted in her ability to maneuver as required by these Rules and is therefore unable to keep out of the way of another vessel.
source_quote: means a vessel which from the nature of her work is restricted in her ability to maneuver as required by these Rules and is therefore unable to keep out of the way of another vessel.

question: What does the word underway mean?
expected_answer: A vessel is not at anchor, or made fast to the shore, or aground.
source_quote: (i) The word underway means that a vessel is not at anchor, or made fast to the shore, or aground.

question: What signal must a vessel give when it is in doubt about the intentions or actions of an approaching vessel?
expected_answer: At least five short and rapid blasts on the whistle.
source_quote: the vessel in doubt shall immediately indicate such doubt by giving at least five short and rapid blasts on the whistle.

question: What is the minimum range of visibility of a masthead light on a vessel of 50 meters or more in length?
expected_answer: 6 miles
source_quote: (a) In vessels of 50 meters or more in length: − a masthead light, 6 miles;

question: How long is a prolonged blast under the Inland Rules?
expected_answer: A blast of from 4 to 6 seconds’ duration.
source_quote: (c) The term prolonged blast means a blast of from 4 to 6 seconds’ duration.

question: In restricted visibility, what does a power-driven vessel underway but stopped and making no way through the water sound, and how often?
expected_answer: Two prolonged blasts in succession with an interval of about 2 seconds between them, at intervals of not more than 2 minutes.
source_quote: (b) A power-driven vessel underway but stopped and making no way through the water shall sound at intervals of not more than 2 minutes two prolonged blasts in succession with an interval of about 2 seconds between them.

question: When power-driven vessels in sight of one another manoeuvre, what does one short blast mean under the International Rules and under the Inland Rules?
expected_answer: International: “I am altering my course to starboard”. Inland: “I intend to leave you on my port side”.
source_quote: − one short blast to mean “I am altering my course to starboard”; | (1) One short blast to mean “I intend to leave you on my port side”;

question: What light may supplement manoeuvring whistle signals and what is its minimum range under the International and Inland Rules?
expected_answer: International: an all-round white light visible at a minimum range of 5 miles. Inland: one all-round white or yellow light visible at a minimum range of 2 miles.
source_quote: the light used for this signal shall, if fitted, be an all-round white light, visible at a minimum range of 5 miles | The light used for this signal shall, if fitted, be one all-round white or yellow light, visible at a minimum range of 2 miles

question: Do both the International and Inland Rules define a vessel constrained by her draft?
expected_answer: International: yes, a power-driven vessel which, because of her draft in relation to the available depth and width of navigable water, is severely restricted in her ability to deviate from the course she is following. Inland: no, paragraph (h) is [Reserved].
source_quote: (h) The term vessel constrained by her draft means a power-driven vessel which | (h) [Reserved]

question: How far away must the top white light of a big ship (50 m or longer) be visible?
expected_answer: 6 miles
source_quote: (a) In vessels of 50 meters or more in length: − a masthead light, 6 miles;

question: What horn signal do I give if I do not understand what the other ship is doing?
expected_answer: At least five short and rapid blasts on the whistle.
source_quote: the vessel in doubt shall immediately indicate such doubt by giving at least five short and rapid blasts on the whistle.

question: What must the fundamental frequency of the whistle be for a vessel 200 meters or more in length?
expected_answer: Between 70-200 Hz.
source_quote: (i) 70-200 Hz, for a vessel 200 meters or more in length;

question: Under the Inland Rules, which flashing white light is a distress signal?
expected_answer: A high intensity white light flashing at regular intervals from 50 to 70 times per minute.
source_quote: (p) A high intensity white light flashing at regular intervals from 50 to 70 times per minute.

question: Which items does the Coast Guard not regulate?
expected_answer: Anchors, paddles, rearview mirrors, or diver/ski flags.
source_quote: The Coast Guard does not regulate anchors, paddles, rearview mirrors, or diver/ski flags.

question: What must the owner of a documented recreational vessel mark on the hull?
expected_answer: The name and hailing port of the vessel together in one place on the hull (usually on the stern).
rule: Documented Vessel Marking Requirements and Hull Display (46 CFR 67.123)
source_quote: Mark the name and hailing port of the vessel together in one place on the hull (usually on the stern).

question: What conditions must pyrotechnic visual distress signals meet?
expected_answer: U.S. Coast Guard-approved, not expired, in serviceable condition, and readily accessible.
source_quote: Pyrotechnic visual distress signals must be U.S. Coast Guard-approved, not expired, in serviceable condition, and readily accessible.

question: What is the minimum height of the letters and numbers of the registration number displayed on a vessel?
expected_answer: Not less than 3 inches in height.
source_quote: Lettering must be in plain, vertical block characters of not less than 3 inches in height.

question: When do pyrotechnic visual distress signals expire?
expected_answer: 42 months after the date of manufacture.
source_quote: Check the expiration date (42 months after the date of manufacture).

question: What size of oil discharge placard must vessels 26 feet and greater in length with machinery spaces display?
expected_answer: At least 5 by 8 inches.
source_quote: Vessels 26 feet and greater in length, with machinery spaces, must display a placard at least 5 by 8 inches

question: How long are boat flares good for after they are made?
expected_answer: 42 months after the date of manufacture.
source_quote: Check the expiration date (42 months after the date of manufacture).

question: How tall do the numbers on the side of my boat have to be?
expected_answer: Not less than 3 inches in height.
source_quote: Lettering must be in plain, vertical block characters of not less than 3 inches in height.

question: What is the controlling depth of a channel?
expected_answer: The least known depth of a channel as determined by hydrographic surveys; it restricts the safe use of the channel to drafts less than that depth.
source_quote: (26) The controlling depth is the least known depth of a channel as determined by hydrographic surveys and restricts the safe use of the channel to drafts less than that depth.

question: What does squat mean?
expected_answer: A change in trim of a ship underway, relative to her trim when stopped.
source_quote: (36) Squat denotes a change in trim of a ship underway, relative to her trim when stopped.

question: From what level are the vertical clearances of bridges and overhead cables given?
expected_answer: In feet above mean high water unless otherwise stated.
source_quote: (17) Vertical clearances of bridges and overhead cables are in feet above mean high water unless otherwise stated

question: How long is a nautical mile?
expected_answer: One minute of latitude, or approximately 2,000 yards; about 1.15 statute miles.
source_quote: A nautical mile is one minute of latitude, or approximately 2,000 yards, and is about 1.15 statute miles.

question: When is settlement appreciable?
expected_answer: When the depth is less than seven times the draft of the ship.
source_quote: Settlement is appreciable when the depth is less than seven times the draft of the ship

question: Which ships must guard VHF channel 13 in addition to VHF channel 16 within U.S. territorial waters?
expected_answer: All ships of length 20m or greater.
source_quote: All ships of length 20m or greater are required to guard VHF channel 13, in addition to VHF channel 16, when operating within U.S. territorial waters.

question: Roughly how many yards are in one nautical mile?
expected_answer: Approximately 2,000 yards.
source_quote: A nautical mile is one minute of latitude, or approximately 2,000 yards, and is about 1.15 statute miles.

question: In simple words, what is squat?
expected_answer: A change in trim of a ship underway, relative to her trim when stopped.
source_quote: (36) Squat denotes a change in trim of a ship underway, relative to her trim when stopped.
